headline: Meta's Muse agent shops from the Shopify catalogue — not from the Meta feed we optimise
intro: Catch-up edition: the daily run had not shipped since 18 Sep (fixed today), so this covers 18–28 Sep with Muse as the lead.

items.title: Meta's Muse agent now shops for US consumers — Walmart, Gap, Sephora, Wayfair and the whole Shopify catalogue
items.what: Muse (launched 8 Sep, US-only, free tier plus paid plans) browses, fills forms and buys on the user's behalf, paying through Stripe Link, with Shop Pay and PayPal added at Connect on 23 Sep. Meta says it launched 'with access to the entire Shopify catalogue' and is adding Walmart, Best Buy, American Eagle, DICK'S, Fanatics, Gap, Michael Kors, Sephora, Ulta and Wayfair as shopping connectors; Zuckerberg says Meta will earn 'a small fee from transactions', not ads.
items.sowhat: A new shopping surface whose product data does not come from Commerce Manager. Meta has published no ranking logic, so nobody can promise a client placement — but every US-market call this week should cover what the agent reads (next item) and that UK shoppers cannot use it yet. A retailer not on Shopify reaches Muse only through a bespoke connector on muse.ai/platform or by being browsed.

items.title: What Muse actually reads: the Shopify product record, shared with Meta by default
items.what: Meta now sits with the other AI channels under Sales channels › Agentic in the Shopify admin, and products are shared with Meta by default through Shopify Catalog for stores selling to the US, Canada or Mexico. Shopify Catalog syndicates title, description, options, images, price and availability from the product record (custom data via metafield mapping); direct checkout is on by default and excludes subscriptions, bundles and customisable products.
items.sowhat: The attributes we engineer into the Meta catalogue feed — colour, material, size, fit — do not reach Muse unless they also live in Shopify options or metafields, so for any client with a US-facing Shopify store the ask is a Shopify data pass, not a feed rule. Check each client's platform before asserting anything; subscription ranges of the YuMOVE kind are excluded from direct checkout by rule.

items.title: Google has removed free product listings from Search across the EEA
items.what: Over 17–18 Sep the unpaid product listings and 'popular products' carousels disappeared from Google Search in EEA countries, which Google's Ads Liaison confirmed follows the July Digital Markets Act decision (a €460m fine over self-preferencing in Search results). Paid Shopping ads are unaffected; trackers cited by Search Engine Roundtable report near-total drops in Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium and Sweden.
items.sowhat: Reiss's EU markets, Superdry's DE/FR/NL/ES/DK/BE/IE feeds and Schuh DE/IE lose the organic half of Shopping; the UK and Reiss CH sit outside the EEA. Expect 'where did the free clicks go' questions — the answer is a paid-coverage and comparison-shopping-service conversation, not a feed fix.

items.title: Google switched on native checkout in AI Mode and Gemini for eligible US Shopify stores — opt-out, not opt-in
items.what: Merchant Center emails on 22 Sep told merchants their Shopify store had been matched to their Merchant Center account, 'enabling native checkout on Google AI Mode and Gemini', with eligible products included automatically. Shopify's help page confirms direct checkout is active by default for US stores selling to US customers, carries no fees beyond payment processing, excludes subscriptions and bundles, and is turned off under Sales channels › Agentic.
items.sowhat: The Buy button reads Merchant Center price and availability, so a mismatch becomes a failed order rather than a disapproval — feed freshness is now a checkout issue. US stores on Shopify only: check Reiss US, Superdry US and House of Bruar US before saying anything either way.

items.title: Merchant API now takes product reviews data sources
items.source: Google Merchant Center Help (reported by Search Engine Roundtable, 18 Sep)
items.what: Google's help page now offers 'Add product reviews using API': product reviews data sources can be uploaded and managed through the Merchant API alongside URL fetch, SFTP and file upload. Product Ratings still needs the interest form, at least 50 reviews and a monthly full data source, and the endpoint is the v1alpha reviews surface, not GA.
items.sowhat: Review-rich clients such as Schuh, Superdry and Reiss can have their product-ratings feed automated off the review platform rather than dropped by file — worth scoping as a one-off setup, with the alpha status stated.

items.title: Meta Graph API v20.0 was removed on 24 Sep; Marketing API v24.0 has until 6 Oct
items.what: Meta's version table lists Graph API v20.0 as available until 24 September 2026 and Marketing API v24.0 as available until 6 October 2026.
items.sowhat: Any catalogue, product-set or feed-upload automation pinned to v20 stopped being supported this week, and anything on Marketing API v24 has eight days — a one-line check with the FeedHero and tech teams on which versions the integrations call.

items.title: Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com
items.what: Muse users reaching Amazon.com see a notice that 'continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use'; Amazon says Meta did not notify it and that the agent does not identify itself. Meta has said Muse has no visibility into people's passwords or payment methods.
items.sowhat: Agent-led demand can be refused by the retailer, so 'can Muse buy from us' is answered by a client's platform and terms, not by the feed. For clients also selling on Amazon, the marketplace listing stays outside Muse for now.

items.title: Google's September Demand Gen Drop puts a Business Agent on video ads that carry product feeds
items.what: Google's monthly Demand Gen update adds a conversational Business Agent to YouTube video ads that carry product feeds (beta sign-up), one-tap image ads on Shorts and Gmail, and affiliate location extensions in Maps.
items.sowhat: Demand Gen product-feed campaigns run off the same Merchant Center data we maintain, so the feed quality work carries straight over; a peak-season test candidate for accounts already running Google and Meta side by side, such as YuMOVE.
